subject: Audit log access, retention & exportability — clarifications and sample request
messages:
From: Amira Qureshi <amira@lynxbank.com>
To: Sofia Ivanova <sofia@redwood.com>
Cc: LynxBank Legal <legal@lynxbank.com>, security@lynxbank.com
Date: Mon, 14 Jul 2025 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Audit log exportability / retention Qs for RFP (LynxBank)

Hi Sofia —

Thanks for the materials you sent earlier. LynxBank's procurement and security teams have a handful of technical clarifications we need before the next evaluation call:

1) Retention windows — please confirm for each of these data classes what Redwood's standard retention is for Hosted, Dedicated, and Private deployments and whether customers can configure longer windows without code changes:
   - Control plane (auth events, API keys, route config changes)
   - Inference request/response logs (full request & model tokens)
   - Metadata / instrumentation (latency traces, sampling, metrics)

2) Export formats & fidelity — what canonical export formats do you support (NDJSON / Parquet / CSV / tar.gz)? Are ephemeral artifacts (KV cache, temp buffers) excluded?

3) Export delivery — supported delivery mechanisms (cross-account S3, presigned URLs, GCS, SFTP, physical media) and typical lead times for bulk exports (100TB scale if applicable).

4) Tamper evidence & chain-of-custody — do you provide signed manifests, SHA256 checksum manifests, and timestamping? Any support for notarized timestamps or signed attestations?

5) Sampling / on-demand slices — for e-discovery we may ask for day-range slices and statistically representative samples. Can Redwood produce deterministic slices and repeatable sampling queries? We also want to know whether you can produce an index file that maps original request IDs to export files.

6) Timestamps & provenance — timezone normalization, monotonic sequence numbers (if any), and whether you preserve original client-submitted timestamps.

7) Audit evidence delivery SLA — typical commitment windows and whether you support push-based delivery for urgent legal requests.

If possible, please attach a short sample export (redacted) and a retention matrix for our legal/security review.

Thanks — Amira

Amira — thanks for the clear list. Summary answers below; I've attached a short retention matrix and a tiny redacted sample export to illustrate format and manifest layout. If helpful I can also share a short export QA checklist.

High level (short answers) — all items are configurable for Dedicated and Private customers; Hosted defaults are opinionated but we offer enterprise add-ons for extended retention and custom exports.

1) Retention windows (defaults and configurable tiers)
   - Control plane logs:
     * Hosted (default): 180 days for operational metadata, 365 days for admin audit events under enterprise plan
     * Dedicated: configurable; typical SLA-backed options: 1 year (standard), up to 7 years (contract)
     * Private (on-prem/VPC): customer-controlled — retention is set by your policy (we provide tooling to snapshot and export)

   - Inference request/response logs (full request bodies and token streams):
     * Hosted (default): 90 days (redactable on request)
     * Dedicated: 1 year typical, up to 3 years with commit
     * Private: fully customer-controlled

   - Metadata / instrumentation (metrics, traces):
     * Hosted: 30–90 days depending on telemetry tier (metrics retained longer in rollup form)
     * Dedicated/Private: configurable, metrics rollups can be retained for years per contract

Notes: retention settings in Hosted can be extended via an add-on. For Dedicated we can bake retention profile into the capacity contract. Private installs have no platform-imposed limits other than local storage.

2) Export formats & fidelity
   - Supported canonical formats: NDJSON (line-delimited JSON), Parquet (columnar), gzipped tarball of NDJSON, and CSV for lightweight metadata tables.
   - We preserve request/response token sequences and timestamps in NDJSON exports. KV cache and transient in-memory buffers are excluded. Exports include a manifest (see attached) that maps logical IDs to files and offsets.

3) Export delivery
   - Supported delivery mechanisms: cross-account S3 (recommended), GCS buckets, Azure Blob, presigned URLs, SFTP over TLS. For very large exports we offer staged delivery (multipart upload + signed manifest) and can arrange AWS Snowball-type physical egress with legal/ops coordination.
   - Typical lead times: small exports (<= 1TB) within 48–72 hours; bulk exports at 10s of TB scale typically 5–10 business days depending on retention tier and export window. We provide progress updates via the Console and can supply direct S3 endpoints.

4) Tamper evidence & chain-of-custody
   - We provide SHA256 checksum manifests for every archive and an optional signed manifest (Redwood's HSM-signed manifest) for Dedicated and Private customers.
   - Timestamps are RFC3339 with timezone info; we support optional notarized timestamping for extract snapshots (contracted feature).

5) Sampling / on-demand slices
   - Yes — exports are deterministic when you provide cursor parameters (start_time, end_time, request_id range). We can produce repeatable sample slices using a documented sampling seed and query: the same seed + query reproduces the sample.
   - We also provide an index file linking original request IDs to exported archive paths (see attached sample-index.json in the zip).

6) Timestamps & provenance
   - All exported records include: recorded_at (server-received timestamp, RFC3339), client_provided_timestamp (if supplied), and sequence_id (monotonic per-region for ordering).

7) Audit evidence delivery SLA
   - For Hosted customers: standard evidence delivery SLA is 10 business days for full export; expedited options (5 business days or 48–72 hours) are available under enterprise SLA.
   - Dedicated/Private: export SLAs are contractable and can be included in Dedicated commits.

Attachments included with this reply (redacted):
 - redwood_retention_matrix_202507.pdf (matrix summarizing default vs configurable retention per data class)
 - export_schema_examples.ndjson.txt (tiny, redacted NDJSON export showing manifest + records)
 - sample-export-202507.zip (redacted index + manifest; 5MB stub)

I'll leave the legal wording to Ben and Marissa — I flagged the parts of the retention matrix that typically get updated during procurement. Happy to hop on a call to walk through a sample export.

Best,

Sofia / Ben —

Thanks for the quick turnaround, Sofia. A couple of procurement/legal notes based on Lynx's ask:

- For the RFP we should keep Hosted default values in the matrix but add an explicit line: "Extended retention (Hosted) available via paid add-on with SLA and encryption-at-rest guarantee" — helps procurement not request impossible defaults.

- Export lead times: they will likely push for "<= 5 business days for full export" in the RFP. We should offer:
  * Standard: 10 business days (no cost)
  * Expedited: 5 business days (enterprise SLA / fee applies)
  * Emergency: 48–72 hours (legal hold + premium support contract)

- Tamper evidence: offer signed manifests for Dedicated by default and for Hosted as an add-on. That keeps our baseline simple but meets enterprise needs.

I've drafted two short redline sentences we can propose back to LynxBank. If Ben agrees, I can mark the redlines in the retention_matrix PDF and send it back to Amira.
